terms.comment: Literally “something for something”. Not ancient: it was the apothecaries’ term for one drug given in place of another, as Bacon says (quid prō quō, ut vocant, Novum organum 2). The English sense, a favour in return, is later.
terms.gloss: one advantage in exchange for another

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
